The President's War

The Smiley Face Army is at war with The Gedagedigedagedago Empire, The French Empire and three more rival nations. You are the President.

Rules

Online battle

Country against country. You command your army from the office or fight on the field; your opponent commands theirs.

SMFA account

One account saves your progress online, keeps you logged in on this device, and holds everything you buy in the Store. No email needed.

SMFA Store

How will you pay?

Nothing is charged by the game. You pay the President directly; the item unlocks on your account when the President approves the order.

President's Desk

Approve cash and GoPay orders, generate codes, grant or revoke items, and see who plays.

Silent shows subtitles only. Synth plays a game-style babble. Speech reads lines aloud with your device's built-in voice. You can also switch it during a cutscene.

Kill cams

Slow-motion cinematic camera for long headshots, enemy commanders and leaders, and vehicles you destroy.

Spoken lines use your device's built-in voice, so they sound different on each device. If your device has no Indonesian voice, Bahasa Indonesia lines are read with the default voice. Grunts, yells and death cries are generated sounds and work everywhere.

How to play

Winning

Destroy the enemy HQ command core (the glowing block inside their HQ), or drain their reinforcement tickets. Holding more than half of the flags drains enemy tickets and earns war budget.

The office (laptop)

Pan W A S D, rotate Q E, zoom with the wheel. Click a squad card or a soldier to select it, then click the map to send it there. Pick a power, then click the target. Tab joins the fight.

In the field (laptop)

Move W A S D, sprint Shift, jump Space, fire with left mouse, aim with right mouse. Weapons: 1 cycles guns (rifle, SMG, shotgun, machine gun, minigun, flamethrower), 2 precision (sniper, railgun, knife), 3 explosives (rockets, grenade launcher, C4, sticky grenades). The mouse wheel or Q scrolls through all of them. G grenade, R reload, E enter or leave a vehicle, Q takes cover, C holds crouch (X toggles it), V switches first and third person, F orders nearby squads to follow you, 4–0 call powers on the crosshair, Tab back to the office.

Vehicles

Tank and jeep: W S drive, A D steer, the mouse aims. Helicopter: W S forward and back, A D turn, Space climb, Shift descend. Rockets and explosives work best against armor.

Cover

Stand next to a wall, sandbags or crates and press Q (COVER on mobile) to snap into cover. Move left and right along it. Behind low cover you pop up when you aim or fire. Behind tall cover, aim near an edge to peek around it, or fire from the middle to blind fire with heavy spread. Enemies struggle to hit you while you stay tucked in. Press Q again, jump, or walk away from the wall to leave cover.

Losing limbs

In Realistic and Sadistic modes a heavy hit, blast or blade can tear off an arm or leg without killing you. One arm: slower reloads and wild aim. No arms: you cannot use weapons. One leg: you limp. No legs: you crawl. Every open wound bleeds until you die, so get to the clinic (the white building with the red cross beside your base): standing there bandages the wounds and heals you, but the limb stays lost. A Medic drop from the office restores limbs fully. In Sadistic mode only, stand next to a severed limb or an enemy corpse and press E (GRAB) to tear off a matching limb and reattach it, enemy uniform and all. Soldiers on both sides suffer the same and will crawl to their own clinic.

Kamikaze

Press K (KAMIKAZE on mobile) in a jet to dive on the biggest enemy crowd and explode. On foot, K sends you sprinting at the nearest enemy group with a bomb; press it again to detonate early. While watching a pilot or soldier from the office, the Kamikaze button orders them to do it. AI soldiers and crippled AI pilots on both sides sometimes decide to go out this way on their own.

World campaign

The campaign is the whole world. The Smiley Face Army starts in Antarctica. The Gedagedigedagedago Empire holds the great powers, the French Empire holds Europe, and the Frowny Federation, the Kingdom of Gloomvania and the Iron Tundra Pact split the rest. Drag and zoom the map, tap a country, and invade any country that borders yours (gold outline) or lies a short hop across the sea. Capitals (★) are big battles. Lose Antarctica and the campaign is over.

Online battles

Press Online battle on the title screen (you need to be logged in). Pick your country, then Quick match to be paired with anyone searching right now, or Create room and send the 5-letter code to a friend, who types it and presses Join. The host's match settings are used. Each of you commands your own army with skirmish rules: capture flags, drain the other side's reinforcements or destroy their HQ core. Matches end after 20 minutes at the latest; the stronger position wins. Leaving or losing connection for 15 seconds counts as a loss. Nukes are off online, and matches shorter than 2 minutes give no rewards.

Victory animations

Win a battle and your President plays a short victory scene. Choose it in Barracks → Victory, where every scene has a Preview button. Parade Salute is free for everyone. Plant the Flag comes with Soldier membership, Three-Point Landing with Sergeant, Don't Look Back with Captain, and The Long Corridor and The Throne Room with General. Every scene can also be unlocked in the Store with SD or Rp, and some come in bundles. Switch them off in Settings if you prefer.

Nuclear warhead

In the campaign, buy it in the Locker room for $15,000. In skirmish, press Buy nuke in the office to buy it with $5,000 of war budget. In skirmish you can launch it whenever you like. In the campaign, the Nuke button only unlocks when you are losing (HQ below half, behind on tickets, or the enemy holds more flags). Type the launch code within 30 seconds; three wrong tries or running out of time locks it for 2 to 3 minutes. On success your squads fall back, and 9 seconds later the blast destroys every soldier, vehicle and building outside the two HQ bunkers. Both HQs are left badly damaged and the battle continues. One nuke per battle. Very rarely, a losing enemy saves up and nukes you: sirens give you 12 seconds to pull your troops back, and the enemy usually forgets to save its own.

Story

The campaign tells the story of the Smiley Face Army's return from exile. As you conquer countries, 3D cutscenes play and story missions unlock in the campaign panel: defend the embassy, rescue a hostage, escort a convoy, kill a general, and storm the Emperor's capital. Heroes such as Reyes (sniper), Okoro (engineer) and Brandt (ace pilot) join and fight in your campaign battles. Tap or press Enter to move through a cutscene, or Skip. Replay them from the campaign panel.

Stealth missions

Some story missions are solo assassinations. Guards have white sight cones; a ? above a guard means they are getting suspicious. Crouch to stay hidden, approach from behind and use the knife for a silent kill. The SMG is suppressed; the sniper rifle is loud. If the alarm goes off the guards hunt you and the target runs for the exit. Kill the target, then return to the drop-off point. No alarm earns the Silent Assassin medal.

Diplomacy

Not every problem needs a war. In the campaign, press Talk next to a nation to propose a ceasefire, trade deal, tribute, peace, an alliance, or the handover of a country. Talks are a debate: read the leader's mood and pick Logic, Pressure, Appeal or Bribe. Proud leaders want respect, greedy ones want money, frightened ones respect strength, cold ones want facts, and angry ones need calm. Each nation remembers how you treat it. Select a country and press Demand surrender: if it surrenders, you secure it with a non-lethal operation where downed enemies are arrested instead of killed. Random world events also ask for your decision between turns.

Navy

The Island Sea map (and island countries in the campaign) is fought across islands. Destroyers, battleships, submarines, carriers and speedboats fight at sea, and landing craft carry squads to the beaches. Soldiers can swim but cannot shoot in the water. Deploy as a speedboat, destroyer or submarine from the deploy menu.

Kill cams and VIPs

Every battle has an enemy commander (★) guarding their HQ, and capitals have the nation's leader (♛). Killing them rewards money and weakens the enemy. Long headshots, commander and leader kills, and vehicles you destroy play a slow-motion kill cam (turn it off in Settings). Earn medals for feats on the Medals screen.

The Long War (campaign story)

Thirty chapters in five acts, launched from the The Long War card on the campaign screen or the chapter list. Chapters are battles, convoy runs, stealth infiltrations, recovery operations and cutscenes. Some cutscenes ask you to decide: those choices are counted as Protector, Strategist, Liberator or Conqueror instincts and, together with your diplomacy, pick one of three endings. Skipping a cutscene never skips a decision. Completed chapters can be replayed without changing your progress; the world map conquest continues alongside the story.

Accounts and the Store

Log in from the title screen (username and password, no email) to save progress online, stay logged in on this device, and use the Store. Smiley Dollars (SD) are earned in every battle and unlock new weapons. Rp items are paid in cash or GoPay directly to the President: place an order, pay, and it unlocks when the President approves it. Codes can be redeemed in the Orders tab. Memberships are 30-day passes with a discount on eligible items; they never change your rank or stats. Nothing in the Store makes you stronger than a free player.

God Mode

A sandbox skirmish for fun. You cannot die, money is unlimited, and nothing is saved and no EXP or medals are earned. Press ⚡ GOD (or B) to open the panel. Pick a tool, then tap a soldier in the office, or shoot one in the field: smite, behead, gib, cut off limbs (Realistic or Sadistic), set on fire, launch, heal, upgrade, make a champion or switch sides. The Spawn tab drops soldiers, squads, extra enemy commanders and leaders, heroes, tanks, helicopters, jets and bombs wherever you tap. The World tab has slow motion, one-hit kills, freezing armies and mass actions. Use Declare victory when you are done.

Special events in skirmish

Choose Kuala Lumpur Twin Towers to fight in the capital city with the towers, or Twin Towers + hijack to have the airliner hijacking strike about a minute in. Bagas flies the plane: dodge the towers to win.

Arcade

Quick 3 to 5 minute matches from the title screen: Waves (survive bigger and bigger attacks with 3 lives), King of the Hill (hold the middle flag to score), Tank Brawl and Dogfight Arena (most vehicle kills in 4 minutes, you respawn automatically). In the campaign, invading a small country plays one of these instead of a full battle.

Barracks and rewards

Every battle earns EXP and Smiley Dollars (SD); medals give a bonus. Levelling up, spending SD and earning medals unlock President outfits, soldier uniforms, helmets, vehicle paint, flag colors, emblems and kill effects like the Abduction Beam. Equip them in the Barracks.

Replays

After a battle, press Watch highlights to see your best moments (headshots, multi-kills, crashes, enemies sent flying) with a cinematic camera, or Full replay to scrub through the whole fight at ¼× to 4× speed. Drag to move the camera, and tap the markers on the timeline to jump to moments.

Saving

Battles autosave every minute and when you switch away from the tab. Press Save battle in the pause menu to save right away, then use Continue battle on the title screen to resume. Finishing or retreating from a battle clears that save. The campaign has three slots. Save codes on the title screen turns your saves into text you can paste on another device.

Deploying and flying

Press Join the fight (Tab) and choose on foot, jeep, tank, helicopter or fighter jet. Each vehicle has a cooldown before you can spawn another. Jets: the mouse (or a drag on mobile) steers the plane toward where you look, W/S set throttle, left click fires guns, right click (MSL) fires a missile once the lock box turns red, G (BOMB) drops bombs onto the red ground marker, R (FLARE) fools incoming missiles. Fly too slow and you stall. E (BAIL) jumps out of a jet or helicopter: press Space (CHUTE) to open your parachute before you hit the ground.

Soldier POV

In the office, select a squad and press Soldier POV (or V) to watch through one soldier's eyes, or Pilot POV to ride in the cockpit of a friendly jet or helicopter. Press Take control (E) to play as that soldier with their own weapon, or Next soldier (N) to switch. Tab returns to the office. If your soldier dies you go back to the office without any penalty.

Voices and captions

Soldiers on both sides call out contacts, reloads, grenades and losses, grunt when hit, and scream when they die. Some say last words. Voices get quieter the farther they are from you. Captions show who said what (green for SMFA, red for the enemy, gold for the President) plus sound cues like [explosion nearby]. Choose the language, captions and voices in Settings.

Difficulty

Easy and Normal enemies react slowly, miss more and rarely call in support. Hard enemies are sharp and hunt the President. Nightmare enemies start trained, upgraded and with extra squads. Harder campaign battles pay more.

Upgrading soldiers

In the office, select a squad and press Upgrade squad. Buy body armor and training (three levels each), or switch the squad's weapon kit: Assault, Heavy, Pyro, Sniper team or Anti-tank. Campaign upgrades such as Veteran academy and Armory carry over to every battle.

Mobile

Left stick moves. WPN opens the weapon list. Drag the right side of the screen to look. Hold FIRE (you can drag on it to aim). RADIO opens powers that hit where you aim. In the office, drag to pan, pinch to zoom, twist with two fingers to rotate, tap to select and order.

Violence modes

Normal: ragdolls only, no blood. Brutal: Normal plus blood. Realistic: double health, better graphics, dismemberment with exposed bone, blood pools, and organs from close explosions. Sadistic: Realistic with heavier gore physics, more organs, exposed ribs and spilled guts. All of it is fictional.
